p: Every great adventure golf round needs a game plan, and the jungle setting here is no exception. Start by taking a quick look at each hole before you play. Look for the slopes, the bumps and the walls you can use to bank a shot. A smooth, gentle putt usually gets you closer than a hopeful thump, and it saves you chasing your ball around the lava.

Agree house rules before you tee off. A six-shot maximum per hole keeps things moving and stops anyone getting stuck, while the youngest players might earn a free second go on the trickier holes. Keeping score is half the fun, but for some families, deciding the score doesn't count at all is the secret to a stress-free afternoon.

Castleford has a few more bits to explore if you want to stretch out the day. Pontefract, a short drive away, is famous for its liquorice and the ruins of its medieval castle, which make for a good wander. RSPB Fairburn Ings, on the edge of town, is a peaceful nature reserve with wetlands and walking trails. And Wakefield's Hepworth gallery is within easy reach for a bit of art.
The beauty of an indoor course is that you can save it for whenever the Yorkshire weather turns. Keep it in your back pocket for those days when outdoor plans are washed out.
